result:
I went through all 150 rules against their docstrings and the shared rules in the module docstring, and fixed 12 that didn't match. I couldn't run any Python in this session, so the fixes are checked only by reading the code and by a text search: the old patterns are gone and the rule 105 edit landed in the right function.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 35 | The 30,000 won cap was applied to the amount before the discount was calculated | Calculate the discount first, then cap it |
| 93 | Same: cap applied to the price, not the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap it |
| 102 | Same: cap applied to the price, not the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap it |
| 45 | Used `round()`, which can round up (shared rule: always round down) | Changed to `// 100` |
| 57 | Used `round()`, which can round up | Changed to `// 100` |
| 115 | Used `round()`, which can round up | Changed to `// 100` |
| 66 | Applied 3% instead of the documented 2% | Changed to 2% |
| 83 | Applied 8% instead of the documented 7% | Changed to 7% |
| 105 | Documented as "marginal" but discounted every unit | Now discounts only units above 30 |
| 107 | Documented as "whole" but discounted only units above 5 | Now discounts every unit |
| 39 | Started at 6 units instead of the documented 5 | Changed to `qty >= 5` |
| 43 | Started at 21 units instead of the documented 20 | Changed to `qty >= 20` |

Rules 39 and 43 only discount units above the threshold, so the discount at exactly the threshold is 0 either way. Prices don't change; I fixed them so the code matches the docstring.

Before relying on this, it's worth running a quick check that compares each `quote(rule_id, qty, unit)` result with the docstring formula, at the threshold and where the cap kicks in.

STATUS: PARTIAL
